md_description: This DAG represents an Arabidopsis thaliana multi-omics workflow in which plants are exposed to altered hormone levels and environmental stress conditions, then profiled by RNA-seq and LC-MS. The pipeline generates transcriptomic and metabolomic signals, converts them into quantitative derivatives, and integrates them with external reference evidence to infer causal interactions between hormone signaling and stress-response pathways.

arabidopsis_thaliana_plants.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I limited fields to intrinsic identity and provenance of the living Arabidopsis study material before any treatment. I excluded treatment parameters, capture settings, raw file properties, computed outputs, and literature/integration fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided sample/experiment identifiers that could be repeated elsewhere in the DAG per the no-duplication rule, and kept only fields that describe what the plants are, where they came from, and their baseline biological state relevant before hormone/stress exposure.

md_schema.descr: Scientific name of the plant material used as the starting biological entity before any hormone or stress treatment; expected to be Arabidopsis thaliana. Use the standard binomial name, e.g. 'Arabidopsis thaliana'.
Common name of the plant entity at the pre-treatment stage, if recorded; typically 'thale cress'. This is an intrinsic label for human readability, not a treatment or measurement output.
Taxonomic identifier for the plant species at the entity level; record as an NCBI Taxonomy or equivalent stable ID, e.g. '3702' for Arabidopsis thaliana.

Baseline developmental stage of the living Arabidopsis plants before treatment, as this defines the biological starting material. Report using a standard growth-stage description or staging system, e.g. seedling, rosette, bolting, flowering.

Age of the plants at the time they entered the workflow, measured in days after germination or planting, depending on the experiment's convention. Typical values are positive integers such as 7, 14, or 21 days.

Brief description of the pre-treatment growth environment that defines the entity's provenance, such as growth chamber, short-day photoperiod, or soil vs. agar culture. Include only baseline cultivation context, not the applied stress treatment.
Genetic background of the Arabidopsis entity before treatment, if a specific accession or mutant line was used. Examples include 'Col-0' or a named mutant line.
Source or provenance of the plant material, such as laboratory stock, seed stock center, or internal colony, if known. Use this to document where the living entity originated before treatment.

Observed baseline health or vigor of the plants before exposure to hormones or stress, recorded as an entity-level quality descriptor. Allowed values should reflect the pre-treatment condition only, e.g. healthy, stressed, mixed, or unknown.

hormone_stress_treatment.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the treatment/protocol parameters that define how plants were exposed to altered hormone levels and environmental stress. I excluded plant identity/provenance fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded capture, raw signal, and downstream computed result fields because they belong to later nodes. I also avoided duplicating any fields already generated for the plant entity, and focused on the minimum operational details needed to reproduce the treatment conditions and interpret the resulting omics changes.

md_schema.descr: Name of the plant hormone whose level was altered during the treatment step, recorded at the process stage. Examples include auxin, abscisic acid, jasmonic acid, salicylic acid, ethylene, or gibberellin.

Direction of the hormone manipulation applied to the plants during this process, indicating whether the hormone level was increased, decreased, or otherwise perturbed relative to the control condition.
Method used to alter hormone levels at the process stage, such as exogenous spray, root drench, media supplementation, vapor exposure, or genetic/chemical inhibition of endogenous signaling.

Final concentration of the applied hormone or hormone analog during treatment, measured at the time of exposure. Use millimolar units where applicable; typical values may range from nanomolar-equivalent low doses to low-millimolar high doses depending on the compound.
Environmental stress condition applied in the treatment step. Record the primary stressor used to challenge the plants during this process.

Operational severity level of the applied environmental stress during the process, as defined by the experimenter. Use a categorical scale such as mild, moderate, or severe, or record control if no stress was applied.

Duration of the environmental stress exposure during this process, measured in minutes from onset of the applied stress until return to normal conditions or sampling. Typical values may range from minutes to hours converted to minutes.

Description of whether hormone alteration and stress exposure were applied separately, simultaneously, or in a factorial combination during this process. This captures the experimental design of the treatment step itself.

Replicate identifier or replicate index for the treatment process, used to distinguish repeated exposure batches under the same hormone and stress condition. Use an integer replicate count such as 1, 2, or 3.
Brief process-level note on the outcome of the treatment step, such as successful exposure, partial response, or aborted treatment, when relevant for reproducibility or data interpretation.

treated_plant_samples.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I captured only intrinsic post-treatment sample properties that define what the treated biological material is before any measurement. I excluded the upstream treatment protocol details because they belong to the hormone_stress_treatment Process, and I excluded RNA-seq/LC-MS capture settings, raw files, and downstream matrices because they belong to later nodes. I also avoided repeating plant identity fields already generated for the source Arabidopsis entity, and focused on the sample state, derived treatment identity, and handling context needed to understand the material entering omics capture.

md_schema.descr: Type of biological material represented by the treated entity before omics measurement, e.g. whole plant, rosette tissue, leaf tissue, root tissue, or pooled tissue. This describes the sample itself, not the collection procedure.
Physical state of the plant material at the time it becomes the treated sample entity, such as intact plant, excised tissue, flash-frozen tissue, or homogenized material prior to capture.

Short summary of the post-treatment phenotype or physiological state observed in the treated plant sample before omics measurement, such as visible stress response, wilting, chlorosis, or no obvious phenotype. This is an entity-level description of the sample state after exposure.

Combined label describing the treatment identity carried by this sample entity, formed from the altered hormone and applied stress condition, e.g. 'ABA_salt' or 'jasmonate_cold'. Use a concise string identifier for the sample's condition class.

Time elapsed from the start of hormone/stress exposure to when this treated sample entity was collected for omics measurements, measured in hours. Typical values may range from minutes converted to fractional hours through several days.
Method used to preserve the treated sample entity before RNA-seq or LC-MS capture, such as flash freezing in liquid nitrogen or immediate stabilization reagent, if applied prior to measurement.

Storage temperature of the treated sample entity prior to omics capture, measured in degrees Celsius, if the sample was held before measurement. Typical values include -80, -20, or 4 depending on the workflow.

Biological replicate identifier for the treated plant sample entity, used to distinguish independently prepared samples under the same treatment condition. Record as a stable string such as 'rep1' or 'bio_03'.

Brief note describing the physical integrity or suitability of the treated sample for downstream capture, such as intact, partially degraded, or suitable for omics. This is a pre-capture sample quality description.

rna_seq_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields for the RNA-seq acquisition itself. I excluded treated plant/sample identity and condition fields because those belong to the upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded raw FASTQ/file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also included hardware manufacturer/model/serial-number style fields per the rules for operation nodes, plus the minimal RNA-seq configuration parameters needed to reproduce the capture and assess its technical quality.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for RNA-seq capture at the measurement session level, such as Illumina. Record the hardware vendor controlling this capture step.
Model name or designation of the sequencing instrument used for RNA-seq capture, e.g. NovaSeq 6000, HiSeq 4000, or equivalent. This identifies the configured hardware for the acquisition session.
Serial number or other unique hardware identifier for the sequencing instrument used during RNA-seq capture. Use the vendor-assigned identifier, e.g. 'SN12345678'.
Sequencing library preparation kit used immediately before or during RNA-seq capture, if applicable. Record the kit name and version as used in this measurement session.

Library strandedness setting configured for RNA-seq capture, indicating whether transcript orientation information was preserved. Typical options are unstranded, stranded, or reverse-stranded depending on the library kit.
Configured read length for the RNA-seq capture, measured in bases per read. Typical values are 50, 75, 100, 150, or paired-end configurations reported per read length.
Read layout used for the RNA-seq capture session, describing whether the instrument acquired single-end or paired-end reads.
Target number of reads planned or achieved for this RNA-seq capture session, measured as total reads per sample or lane. Typical values are in the millions to tens of millions.
Date on which the RNA-seq capture session was performed. Record the acquisition date for the sequencing run as a calendar date.
Whether the RNA-seq capture session completed successfully and produced usable sequencing output. This is a technical session-level status flag, not a property of the file itself.
Calibration or maintenance status of the sequencing instrument immediately before the capture session, as recorded by the operator. Use this to document whether the hardware was fit for acquisition.

raw_rna_seq_fastq.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw-data artefact properties of the FASTQ file(s): format, size, read structure, and technical quality metrics. I excluded capture settings such as instrument, library prep, read length, and run date because those belong to the RNA-seq Capture node, and I excluded alignment or expression quantities because those belong to downstream Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided any sample or treatment descriptors already assigned upstream, and focused on the minimum file-level metadata needed to store, validate, and reuse the raw sequencing artefact.

md_schema.descr: Raw data file format for the RNA-seq signal artefact, expected to be FASTQ. Record the actual file container used for the sequencing reads.
Size of the raw FASTQ file in bytes at the time of storage or ingestion. Typical values may range from millions to billions of bytes depending on read depth and compression.
Total number of sequencing reads contained in the raw FASTQ signal file, measured after demultiplexing if applicable. Typical values are in the millions for RNA-seq datasets.
Total number of base calls represented in the raw FASTQ file, measured across all reads in the file. Typical values depend on read length and read count and are usually very large integers.
Average Phred quality score across bases in the raw FASTQ reads, used as a technical quality metric for the signal artefact. Typical RNA-seq values are often in the high 20s to 30s.
Whether the raw FASTQ signal passed a predefined per-base sequencing quality threshold during QC. This is a file-level technical flag, not a biological interpretation.
Whether adapter sequence contamination was detected in the raw FASTQ artefact during technical QC. Use this to indicate if adapter trimming may be required downstream.
Fraction of duplicate reads observed in the raw FASTQ signal file, measured as a technical quality metric prior to alignment. Typical values range from 0 to 1.
Storage location or URI for the raw FASTQ artefact, such as a file path, object-store URI, or accession location. Example formats include 's3://bucket/file.fastq.gz' or '/data/run1/sample.fastq.gz'.
MD5 checksum for the raw FASTQ file, used to verify file integrity after transfer or storage. Record as a 32-character hexadecimal string when available.

rna_seq_alignment.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only alignment workflow parameters and software-agent details that define how the raw RNA-seq Signal is transformed into quantified transcript evidence. I excluded raw FASTQ file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting expression matrix dimensions or values because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating generic treatment/sample metadata already captured upstream, and focused on the minimum reproducible alignment settings and output QC indicators for this process step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used for RNA-seq alignment in this process step, recorded at the operation-node level. Example: 'STAR'.
Version of the RNA-seq alignment software used in this process step, such as '2.7.x'. Record the exact version to support reproducibility of the alignment workflow.
Repository, download source, or code reference for the alignment software used in this process step, such as a GitHub URL or vendor distribution source.
Arabidopsis reference genome assembly used as the alignment target in this process step, e.g. TAIR10 or a specified genome build. Record the exact assembly version used to map reads.
Gene annotation release used during alignment and transcript quantification, such as a GTF/GFF version or release label corresponding to the chosen Arabidopsis genome build.
Operational mode used for read mapping in this process step, describing whether reads were aligned as single-end, paired-end, or with transcriptome-guided settings.
Maximum allowed mismatch fraction or equivalent alignment tolerance configured for this process, if specified. Use a numeric fraction between 0 and 1 to describe permissiveness of read mapping.
How reads that align to multiple loci were handled during this process step, such as discarded, assigned probabilistically, or retained according to a specified rule.

Minimum mapping quality threshold applied during the RNA-seq alignment or post-alignment filtering stage, measured on the aligner's internal quality scale. Typical values are nonnegative integers such as 10, 20, or 30.

Proportion of raw reads successfully aligned to the Arabidopsis reference genome during this process step. Record as a fraction from 0 to 1, representing the key output quality indicator for alignment.
Number of reads that passed alignment and were retained for downstream quantification in this process step. This is a process output summary metric, not a file property.
Wall-clock runtime of the alignment process, measured in minutes from job start to completion. Typical values depend on data size and compute resources.

gene_expression_matrix.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result fields that describe the gene expression matrix itself: what algorithmic form it takes, its dimensions, normalization state, value scale, and result-level QC. I excluded the alignment software and reference genome parameters because those belong to the upstream RNA-seq alignment Process, and I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the Signal node. I also avoided sample identity and treatment descriptors already handled upstream, and focused on the minimum metadata needed for users to interpret, reuse, and compare the derived expression table.

md_schema.descr: Type of computed gene expression table produced from aligned RNA-seq data, indicating whether values are raw counts, normalized counts, TPM, FPKM, or another quantified form. This describes the derivative representation of the data matrix.

Algorithm or counting approach used to derive the gene-by-sample matrix from aligned reads, such as featureCounts, HTSeq, or a custom pipeline. Record the method used to compute the derivative values.

Number of gene features represented as rows in the expression matrix, measured after filtering and aggregation. Typical values correspond to the number of annotated Arabidopsis genes retained for analysis.
Number of sample columns in the gene expression matrix, representing the biological samples included in this derivative table.

Normalization method applied to the expression matrix values, if any, such as library-size scaling, TPM normalization, or variance-stabilizing transformation. Record the transformation used on the derivative values.
Whether a logarithmic transform was applied to the expression values in this derivative matrix, such as log2(count+1) or similar. This is a computed-result formatting property.
Fraction of matrix entries that are non-zero after quantification and any filtering, measured as a summary of sparsity for the derivative table. Typical values range from 0 to 1.

Minimum numeric expression value observed in the matrix after any normalization or transformation, used as a quick summary of the derivative range. Report in the units or scale of the chosen matrix type.

Maximum numeric expression value observed in the matrix after any normalization or transformation, used as a quick summary of the derivative range. Report in the units or scale of the chosen matrix type.

Annotation source used to define the gene features in this derivative matrix, such as TAIR or a specific Arabidopsis annotation release. This identifies the feature universe used for the computed output.
Overall quality status assigned to the computed expression matrix after generation and filtering, indicating whether it is suitable for downstream analysis.

lc_ms_capture.reasoning: I removed all fields that collided with already_generated across the DAG: generic instrument identity fields and run-level status/date fields. I kept only LC-MS capture-specific configuration parameters that remain within this node's semantic territory and are not duplicated elsewhere. These fields describe the acquisition setup for the metabolomics measurement session without repeating sample, raw data, or downstream derivative content.

md_schema.descr: Type of chromatographic column used for LC separation during the LC-MS capture session, such as C18 reverse phase, HILIC, or another configured column chemistry. This is a measurement-session configuration parameter.
Mobile phase solvent composition used for LC separation in this capture step, described as the configured solvent system or main additives. Include the operational composition relevant to the run.
Liquid chromatography flow rate used during the capture session, measured in milliliters per minute. Typical values are often in the 0.1 to 1.0 mL/min range depending on the method.
Chromatography column temperature during the LC-MS capture session, measured in degrees Celsius. Typical values may range from ambient to around 60 Celsius depending on the method.
Ionization polarity and mode used for mass spectrometric acquisition in this capture session. Typical options include positive and negative electrospray ionization.
Mass analyzer type used for the MS portion of the capture session, such as Orbitrap, time-of-flight, ion trap, or quadrupole. This identifies the acquisition hardware configuration.
Configured mass-to-charge range scanned during LC-MS acquisition, reported as the instrumental m/z window for this capture session, e.g. 50-1000 m/z.
Acquisition scan rate for the LC-MS session, measured in scans per second (Hz). Typical values depend on the instrument and method and may range from low to tens of scans per second.
Ion source temperature used during the LC-MS capture session, measured in degrees Celsius. This setting affects desolvation and ionization efficiency at the instrument stage.

Collision energy applied during tandem MS or in-source fragmentation settings for this capture session, measured in electron volts. Report the configured value used during acquisition when applicable.

Name or identifier of the LC-MS acquisition method used for this capture session, such as a vendor method file name or lab-specific method code. Use a stable string identifier for the configured run method.
Brief operator note about the LC-MS capture session, including any deviations from the standard method that affected acquisition settings but are not already captured in structured fields.

raw_lc_ms_spectra.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I kept only raw LC-MS artefact properties specific to the spectra file and avoided all upstream capture details and downstream feature/derivative fields. I also removed the colliding generic file-level fields that were already generated elsewhere in the DAG, and replaced them with LC-MS-specific raw-signal descriptors that do not repeat prior metadata. The remaining fields describe the technical structure and quality of the raw chromatographic/mass spectral artefact itself, which is the correct semantic territory for this node.

md_schema.descr: Acquisition mode encoded in the raw LC-MS signal file, such as full scan or data-dependent acquisition. This is a file-level raw-signal property describing the structure of the captured spectra.
Encoding or storage representation used for the raw LC-MS signal data within the file, such as profile, centroid, or mixed. This describes the form of the raw spectral artefact.
Total number of MS scans contained in the raw LC-MS signal artefact, measured across the entire acquisition run. This is a file-level structural property of the spectra and chromatogram record.

Total number of retention-time samples or chromatographic points represented in the raw LC-MS artefact after conversion to the chosen file format. This captures the time-axis resolution of the raw signal.
Number of distinct mass spectra present in the raw LC-MS signal file. This reflects the amount of spectral content stored in the raw artefact.
Average signal-to-noise ratio across the raw LC-MS spectra, used as a technical quality metric for the signal artefact. Typical values vary by instrument and sample complexity.
Estimated mass accuracy of the raw LC-MS signal in parts per million, used as a file-level technical quality indicator. Lower values indicate tighter mass measurement precision.
Fraction of expected scans missing or unusable in the raw LC-MS artefact, measured as a technical completeness metric. Values should range from 0 to 1.
Whether peak picking or centroiding was applied in the raw LC-MS signal representation before storage. This indicates the level of preprocessing present in the artefact itself.
Total ion count represented by the raw LC-MS artefact across the acquisition run, as a technical summary of signal abundance. This is a file-level summary metric of the raw spectra.

metabolite_feature_extraction.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I kept only metabolite feature extraction parameters and process-level quality indicators, while removing the software-agent fields that collide with prior Process nodes in the DAG. I excluded raw LC-MS capture and signal properties because they belong upstream, and I excluded the downstream abundance table itself because file/output properties belong to the Derivative node. The remaining fields describe the operational settings needed to reproduce peak detection, alignment, summarization, and assess whether the feature extraction output is usable.

md_schema.descr: Algorithm or parameterization used to detect metabolite peaks from the raw LC-MS spectra during this process step, such as centWave, matchedFilter, or an equivalent method.
Method used to align detected metabolite features across samples in this process step, such as retention-time alignment or a specific peak grouping strategy.

Maximum retention-time deviation allowed when aligning features across samples in this process step, measured in seconds. Typical values depend on LC-MS method precision and may range from fractions of a second to several tens of seconds.
Mass-to-charge tolerance used during peak matching or feature alignment in this process step, measured in parts per million. Typical values are often in the low to tens of ppm range.
Method used to handle missing peak intensities during feature summarization in this process step, if applicable. Record the imputation or handling strategy used before producing the abundance table.
Statistic used to summarize peak intensities across scans or across feature traces in this process step, such as apex intensity or integrated area under the peak.
Total number of metabolite features detected by this process step before or after filtering, reported as a process output summary metric.
Fraction of detected features successfully aligned across samples during this process step, measured as a process-level quality indicator between 0 and 1.
Overall technical quality status assigned to the feature extraction process after peak detection and alignment, indicating whether the output is suitable for downstream quantification.

metabolite_abundance_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I kept only result-level fields that are specific to the metabolite abundance table and do not collide with previously generated matrix or QC fields. I excluded upstream LC-MS acquisition and feature extraction details because they belong to Capture and Process nodes, and I avoided repeating generic computed-matrix fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG. The remaining fields describe the table’s content identity, missingness, value range, and annotation provenance, which are sufficient for downstream use without duplicating prior metadata.

md_schema.descr: Type of computed metabolite table produced from LC-MS data, indicating whether the values represent raw peak areas, normalized abundances, or another summarized representation. This describes the derivative matrix format.
Fraction of abundance matrix entries that are missing after feature extraction, alignment, and table construction. Values should range from 0 to 1 and summarize sparsity in the derivative output.
Minimum numeric abundance value observed in the table after normalization or transformation, used as a quick summary of the derivative range. Report on the scale of the chosen matrix type.
Maximum numeric abundance value observed in the table after normalization or transformation, used as a quick summary of the derivative range. Report on the scale of the chosen matrix type.

Annotation source used to identify metabolite features in this derivative table, such as a compound library, mass spectral database, or internal annotation resource. This identifies the feature universe used for the computed output.

Identifier namespace used for metabolite feature rows in the abundance table, such as an internal feature label scheme, HMDB accession, KEGG compound ID, or m/z-retention-time feature key. Use a string example such as 'feature_001' or 'HMDB0000122'.
Type of row identifier used in the metabolite abundance table to distinguish features, recorded at the derivative stage. Examples include internal peak ID, compound accession, or mass-feature key.

Summary of annotation confidence for features in the metabolite abundance table, capturing the typical certainty of metabolite identities assigned to rows in this derivative. Use a short categorical or textual summary such as high, mixed, or low.

external_reference_studies.reasoning: This node is an external Derivative, so I included only metadata that describes the reference evidence set itself: what kind of evidence it contains, where it came from, how it was curated, and basic evidence coverage/quality. I excluded experimental capture/process details because this node is not a wet-lab or measurement step, and I excluded downstream integration or causal inference fields because those belong to the multi-omics integration process and causal output node. I also avoided all colliding derivative-style fields already generated elsewhere, and focused on the minimum provenance and evidence descriptors needed for reuse of the reference set.

md_schema.descr: Curation style used to assemble the external evidence set, describing whether the studies were manually reviewed, automatically extracted, or a hybrid of both. This is a provenance field for the reference derivative.
Name of the literature or database source from which the external reference studies were collected, such as a curated plant biology resource, publication database, or internal knowledge base.
Version, release date, or snapshot identifier of the source database used to compile the reference evidence set. Record the exact release when available to support reproducibility.

Brief description of the search terms, filters, or inclusion criteria used to identify studies relevant to Arabidopsis hormone signaling and stress-response interactions. This documents how the evidence set was derived.

Summary of evidence types represented in the curated set, such as genetics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, biochemical assays, or review-level assertions. This describes the composition of the reference evidence derivative.
Total number of distinct studies or reference records included in the external evidence set. This is a count of curated literature items used as external support.
Species scope covered by the curated evidence set. For this DAG, the primary scope should be Arabidopsis thaliana, but broader scope can be recorded if cross-species evidence was included.

Aggregate confidence score assigned to the curated evidence set, reflecting the curator's overall confidence in relevance and reliability. Use a numeric score on the project's chosen scale, such as 0 to 1.
List of accession identifiers, DOIs, PMIDs, or equivalent stable identifiers for the curated reference studies. Use a delimited string or compact list format to document the evidence items.
Overall quality status for the curated reference evidence set after review, indicating whether the set is suitable for downstream integration and causal inference.

multiomics_integration.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I kept only integration-specific parameters and quality indicators that describe how the omics derivatives and external evidence are combined. I removed the colliding software_* fields because they were already generated on earlier process nodes in this DAG. I also excluded upstream derivative properties and downstream causal output properties, since those belong to input/output nodes rather than the integration process itself.

md_schema.descr: High-level strategy used to combine transcriptomic derivatives, metabolomic derivatives, and external reference evidence during this process step, such as correlation-based integration, network-based inference, or causal graph scoring.
Rule or weighting scheme used to incorporate external reference studies into the integration analysis, such as equal weighting, confidence-weighted, or evidence-prioritized scoring.
Rule used to pair hormone-level changes with stress-response signatures during the integration step, for example same-sample pairing, condition-level aggregation, or pathway-level matching.

Threshold used to retain candidate causal interactions in this integration step, measured on the model's internal scoring scale. Typical values depend on the method and should be recorded exactly as used.
Statistical correction method applied to tests or scores within the integration step, if used, such as Benjamini-Hochberg or Bonferroni. Record the adjustment procedure for inference control.
Number of candidate causal interactions produced by this integration process before or after filtering, reported as a process output summary metric.
Overall quality status assigned to the integration process after combining omics and reference evidence, indicating whether the result is suitable for downstream reporting.

causal_interaction_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result fields that describe the causal interaction table itself: what kinds of interactions it contains, how many were retained, how strong they are, and the output's format and quality. I excluded upstream integration-method parameters and software details because those belong to the multiomics_integration Process, and I excluded raw/derivative input properties because they belong to earlier nodes. I also avoided any field IDs already generated elsewhere in the DAG, and focused on the minimum metadata needed to interpret and reuse the final integrated causal results.

md_schema.descr: Type of integrated result represented by this derivative table, indicating that it contains causal or evidence-supported interactions among hormones, stress conditions, gene expression changes, and metabolite shifts.

Short description of how an entry in the causal interaction table is defined, such as a hormone-to-gene, gene-to-metabolite, or stress-to-pathway interaction supported by omics and reference evidence. This explains the semantic unit stored in the derivative.
Number of interaction records represented as rows in the causal interaction table after integration and filtering. Typical values depend on the study and may range from a handful to many thousands.
Number of columns in the causal interaction table, representing the variables or annotations retained for each interaction record.
Scale used for the causal interaction score or confidence value in the table, such as 0 to 1 or a project-specific ranking scale. This describes how the derived interaction strength is represented.
Minimum causal score observed in the table after integration and filtering, reported on the chosen score scale. This summarizes the lower bound of the derivative output.
Maximum causal score observed in the table after integration and filtering, reported on the chosen score scale. This summarizes the upper bound of the derivative output.

Number of reference studies, evidence items, or omics-derived supports associated with each interaction or aggregated across the table, depending on the table design. Record the support count used to annotate the causal derivative.
Whether the causal interaction table explicitly encodes directionality, such as hormone-to-stress or gene-to-metabolite arrows. This is a structural property of the derivative output.
File or table format used for exporting the causal interaction derivative, such as TSV, CSV, or another structured text format. Record the actual output serialization format.
Overall quality status assigned to the final causal interaction table after integration, indicating whether the result is suitable for downstream interpretation and reuse.
